summary.text: John Ricottone, a Republican, Conservative and Stop Mamdani Party retired NYPD officer who describes himself as president of Community Education Council District 20, lost the November 3, 2026 election for New York State Assembly District 47 to incumbent William Colton.

paragraphs.text: Ricottone earned a high school diploma from John Dewey High School and an associate degree from Ashworth College in 2005.
He is a retired NYPD officer, and Ballotpedia lists his profession as retired as of 2026.

He describes himself as President of Community Education Council District 20, where he says he worked to improve school safety, helped obtain $50,000 in City Council funding for one of his liaison schools, and pushed for school safety agent hiring and more after-school funding.
Ricottone advanced from the Conservative Party primary on June 23, 2026, and the Republican primary for the seat was canceled.
He was on the November 3, 2026 ballot as the Republican, Conservative and Stop Mamdani Party candidate.
During the campaign, his stated priorities, according to his Ballotpedia survey, were safer and cleaner streets, affordability and education.
In the November 3, 2026 general election, Ricottone lost to William Colton, according to unofficial results from the NYC Board of Elections and Wikipedia.
